podcast.title: Backlash and Removal from Christian Stores
podcast.body: After a "Rolling Stone" interview featured "much swearing," Evanescence faced a "substantial and very, very loud" backlash from the Christian rock community. Consequently, Wind-up Records was compelled to withdraw all of Evanescence's records from Christian stores. "When Rolling Stone published an interview featuring much swearing, the backlash from the Christian rock community was substantial and very, very loud. Wind Up Records was forced to pull all Evan Essence records out of all Christian stores."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Classification as Christian Rock
podcast.body: Due to their spiritual lyricism and occasional references to God, Evanescence became widely classified as a Christian rock band, regardless of their own intentions for this categorization. "The spiritual lyrics and occasional mentions of God were appreciated. And whether they had tended this to happen or not, Evan Essence became classified as a Christian rock band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Controversy and "Fall from Grace"
podcast.body: Following a Rolling Stone interview where band members used profanity, Evanescence faced a significant and vocal backlash from the Christian rock community. This resulted in Wind-up Records being compelled to withdraw all Evanescence records from Christian retail outlets. "When Rolling Stone published an interview featuring much swearing, the backlash from the Christian rock community was substantial and very, very loud."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Christian Classification
podcast.body: Evanescence initially sold a large volume of records through Christian stores, developing a strong fanbase, largely due to their spiritual lyrics and occasional mentions of God. This led to their classification as a Christian rock band, whether it was their explicit intention or not. "And whether they attended this to happen or not, Evan Essence became classified as a Christian rock band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Escaped New Metal Classification
podcast.body: Evanescence was initially categorized under the heading of new metal but eventually escaped that classification, a goal many bands fought hard to achieve. "Evanescence... Most eventually escaped that classification, something that many fought very hard to do."

podcast.title: Formation at Youth Camp
podcast.body: The members of Evanescence initially met and formed the band at a youth camp in Arkansas, indicating early ties to a religious community. "They were formed when members of the band met at a youth camp in Arkansas."

podcast.title: Inspired by Skinny Puppy
podcast.body: Evanescence is explicitly listed as an artist who was inspired and influenced by the Canadian industrial band Skinny Puppy. "Here's a short list of artists who say they were inspired and influenced by Skinny Puppy, Ministry, Nine-inch Nails, Maryland Manson, the Prodigy, Ramstein, Filter, Corn, Lincoln Park, Evan Essence."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Launch Through Christian Market
podcast.body: Following their record deal, Evanescence's CDs were primarily sold through Christian record stores, a common strategy for their label, Wind-up Records, which had similarly launched Creed's career. This distribution method was instrumental in building and solidifying their initial fanbase. "When they signed to a record deal, other CDs were sold through Christian record stores, which is not surprising considering that their record company was wind up, the same label that launched Creed's career in the same way."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Modern Multi-tracking (200+ Tracks)
podcast.body: Evanescence utilized extensive multi-tracking in their music production, with one particular song featuring over 200 tracks. The band reported losing count of the numerous layers involved in creating the mix for this song. This level of multi-tracking stands in stark contrast to earlier recording methods and the opposition faced by multi-track recording innovators in the 1950s. "Evan Essence, 200 plus tracks, went into creating that mix."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Multi-Platinum Success
podcast.body: Evanescence, led by Amy Lee, achieved unexpected multi-platinum success in the early 2000s, though some categorized them on the fringes of new metal. "The surprise, multi-platinum success of Amy Lee and Evan Essence, another group that some insist on placing on the fringes of New Metal."

podcast.title: Ringtone Popularity - Mid-2000s
podcast.body: In the mid-2000s, songs by artists like Evanescence were constantly heard as ringtones in public spaces such as the subway, schools, hospitals, and streets. This reflected a widespread desire among young people to publicly display their musical tastes and individuality. "Canciones de Metallica, Eminem, Fifth Dissent, Blint Note, Linkin Park, The Vanessens, sonaban constantemente en el metro, en el colegio, en el hospital, en la calle."

podcast.title: Shift from Christian Rock Label
podcast.body: While Evanescence started within the Christian rock scene and gained initial traction there, they may no longer be considered part of that world due to their crossover success and subsequent controversies. "They may not be considered to be part of the Christian rock world now, but that's where they started."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Terry Balsamo's Headbanging-Related Stroke
podcast.body: Guitarist Terry Balsamo suffered a stroke while playing for Evanescence, which doctors suspect might have been related to his headbanging on stage. This highlights the potential severe health risks associated with the practice. "While playing guitar for Evan Essence, he had stroke. Doctors think it might have been related to his head banging."

xref.title: "The Woman with the Golden Ears" in A&R
xref.body: Meltzer transitioned into A&R, where she gained a reputation as "The Woman with the Golden Ears" due to her exceptional ability to identify and sign hit acts. Her keen ear led her to sign prominent bands such as Creed, Evanescence, Alter Bridge, Finger 11, Drowning Pool, and Bright Eyes. "And because she was so good at picking hit acts, she became known as the Woman with the Golden Ears."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Extensive Touring After Debut Album
xref.body: The success of "Not Ready To Go" transformed the band's career, leading to relentless touring with "a couple hundred shows a year" in the first few years. They opened for various bands, including Three Days Grace, Evanescence, and Big Sugar, playing in arenas. "suddenly we were getting our first offers to play in arenas opening for bands. And we were on the road all the time, like couple hundred shows a year, easy for those first couple of years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Goth DNA
xref.body: Amy Lee of Evanescence (referred to as F&S) is described as having "definitely Goth in her DNA," suggesting a strong inherent connection to the genre. "Look at Amy Lee of F&S since there's definitely Goth in her DNA."

xref.title: Number One Records in 2010s
xref.body: Fall Out Boy was among the artists, including Blink-182, Green Day, Coldplay, Jack White, Red Hot Chili Peppers, Slipknot, Queens of the Stone Age, Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters, U2, Linkin Park, Evanescence, and David Bowie, who achieved number one records during the 2010s. This demonstrated the continued success of rock acts in an era where hip hop was a dominant cultural force. xref.title: Shirley Manson's Influence
xref.body: Shirley Manson, the Scottish singer drafted into the American band Garbage, has had a notable impact on contemporary artists. Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evanescence, Katy Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish, and Lana Del Rey. "Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evan Essence, Katie Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish and Lana Del Rey."
